evidence.quote: d to provide technique feedback on a climber mid-route would rely mostly on language priors and contextual cues, eliciting only the information that a person is climbing from the video. Such a model would produce common, plausible-sounding but often vague advice such as “Pull your hips closer to the wall”, due to limited attention to the frames that actually reveal the problem. The true technique errors are visible only in the orange frames: the climber starts pulling up, without using proper foot positioning, and straining their arms under their body weight. A well-grounded model would attend to precisely these moments before generating feedback.
